facts.fact: The average website conversion rate across all industries hovers between 2 and 3%, according to a source cited by Outbrain.
facts.quote: Across all industries, the average conversion rate hovers between [2 to 3%](https://www.invespcro.com/blog/the-average-website-conversion-rate-by-industry/).

facts.fact: A Google case study cited by Outbrain reports that retargeting campaigns can result in a conversion uplift of more than 160% in some cases.
facts.quote: Retargeting campaigns can result in a big uplift in conversions, [more than 160% in some cases](https://services.google.com/fh/files/misc/casestudy-rlsa-tirendo.pdf).

facts.fact: Outbrain's own analytics show that visitors spend about five minutes on its site before converting, and Outbrain created a remarketing list for people who spend four minutes on the site in a single visit.
facts.value: 5 minutes (average time before conversion); 4 minutes (list threshold)
facts.quote: For us at Outbrain, it’s about five minutes. So we’ve created a separate remarketing list for those who spend four minutes on our site during a single visit.

facts.fact: Outbrain's third-party tag feature allows retargeting of people who clicked on earned media content recommendations, not only visitors to the advertiser's own site.
facts.quote: unless _you_ install a retargeting pixel that triggers when someone _clicks_ on the content recommendation.

facts.fact: The article lists 13 retargeting tips for using Outbrain's third-party tagging feature.
facts.quote: with the following 13 retargeting tips that will take your digital marketing ROI to the next level

facts.fact: Outbrain states that pixel-based retargeting can start immediately, while list-based retargeting requires constantly updating and segmenting lists.
facts.quote: The advantage of a pixel-based campaign is you can start retargeting people straight away.

facts.fact: Outbrain advises not to retarget people who spend less than 10 seconds on a site, since they likely clicked by accident.
facts.quote: don’t bother retargeting people who spend less than 10 seconds on your site

facts.fact: Outbrain's own retargeting list targets people who visit its case studies page more than once within a 10-day period.
facts.quote: more than once within a 10-day period

facts.fact: Outbrain suggests putting a time limit on a checkout-abandonment coupon offer, noting that 24 hours often works.
Outbrain's author recommends capping retargeting ads at no more than two to three per individual per day.
facts.quote: My recommendation is not more than two to three a day.

facts.fact: Outbrain states that, at the time of writing, only Google allows advertisers to set retargeting frequency and block certain IPs.
facts.quote: At the moment, only Google allows you to set the frequency and block certain IPs

facts.fact: Outbrain serves different content sets based on how long ago a visitor came to its site: days 0-5, days 6-10, and days 11-15.
facts.quote: we use a specific set of content between days zero to five. A new set is used for visitors from between six to 10 days ago. Finally, another set is used for people who visited 11 to 15 days ago.

facts.fact: For an annual subscription, Outbrain suggests pausing the renewal retargeting list for 11 months and activating it in the last month of the subscription.
facts.quote: Simply pause the list for 11 months, then flip the switch when the time comes.

facts.fact: Outbrain's article lists 13 retargeting tactics in its summary.
facts.quote: let’s review the 13 tactics I just covered
